title: shifted-zeta-positivity: computer-assisted positivity for shifted zeta canonical systems (manuscripts, verification records, research log)
description:
Research program around Suzuki's shifted screw functions Ψω and the shifted scattering function Θω(z) = ξ(1/2 − ω − iz)/ξ(1/2 + ω − iz) for the Riemann zeta function: quantitative criteria for zero-free half-planes, the associated inverse-spectral (Krein string / canonical system) family, and computer-assisted positivity certificates on the prime-free first slab.

This record archives the whole repository at a release tag. Released manuscripts live under papers/<slug>/; each has its own CITATION.cff and is additionally deposited as a separate Zenodo record (linked below as has part). The blueprint/ and statements/ directories give the statement inventory of each released paper with dependency graph, proof status, human-verification status and formalization feasibility; verification/ holds referee-round records and independent recomputation scripts; notes/ is the redacted research log.

Release v1.0 contains the preprint Archimedean first-slab positivity for shifted zeta canonical systems: an off-center Weil generator and a radial energy identity (folder papers/first-slab-positivity/) and the material around it. The four other manuscripts (psi-omega-margin, omega-string, defect-depth, rh-detector) are present as clearly labelled working drafts with their reproduction code; they are not released and no DOI covers them as finished work — see each folder's STATUS.md. The rh-detector manuscript is a separate, earlier thread unrelated to the Suzuki program.

Disclosure: the work was produced with substantial language-model assistance and has not yet had line-by-line human verification of its central analytic steps; the per-statement status is recorded in the repository. Nothing here claims progress toward the Riemann hypothesis or a new zero-free region.
notes: Cite a paper in this repository by the version DOI of the release plus its folder path, or by the paper's own Zenodo record (linked as 'has part' once minted). Dual license (see LICENSE): text CC BY 4.0, code MIT. Third-party PDFs are not included.
